meta.useLimits: Sales-design reference. Not purchase-ready SKUs, not engineering or code approval. Rules are reference-only and must not be enforced or ordered from without production verification.
notes: Sales-design presets are owner-approved (D4 FINAL, 11 Nov 2026). Not construction-approved. Structural connections, manufacturer hardware and code compliance are pending verification.
changesV1_1: Added basis/sourceTier to every record; replaced salesVisibility (default/more-options/hidden) with salesListing (listed / listed-with-notice / hold) + salesPriority. No product is held back for being less popular.

D4: in-deck posts defined as wood posts inside the rim framing, extending through the decking with decking cut around them (not surface-mounted bases). Both face-mount and in-deck kept for all four presets as AOS design decisions; attachment, blocking, hold-downs and post spacing remain unverified.

Wood railing styles, finishes and mounting options re-labelled aos-design / aos-decision (were defaulting to verified). IRC numeric values marked secondary-source; MN adoption and guard trigger verified from MN Rules 1309.

D4 FINAL (11 Nov 2026): four presets fully specified (members, balusters, caps, posts, heights, spacing), corners, post caps (flat default / pyramid), stairs and separate 1-1/2 in satin-black handrail, sales behavior rules, owner-entered notes verbatim, open items and compatibility questions. Design choices owner-approved; structure, hardware and code pending verification.

rules.rule: Wood railing lumber is one uniform global choice (green or brown pressure-treated) for all AOS wood deck-edge sections and staircases. No per-edge or per-stair lumber overrides.
Initial lumber default matches green or brown treated decking; with composite/PVC decking it defaults to brown treated. James may change the global railing lumber independently of decking.
If James chose the railing lumber manually, later decking changes preserve that choice (Q5).
One deck-wide default style and baluster infill, with per-edge overrides (T-top/standard; wood/round black aluminum) and per-stair overrides. Lumber is never part of these overrides.
Changing the global style updates only sections still inheriting defaults; customized edges and staircases are not reset.
An explicit Apply to All action, with confirmation, is the only way to overwrite edge/stair customizations.

Product switches preserve deck shape, exact geometry, stairs, perimeter positions, railing locations and unrelated selections; compatible overrides are kept and conflicts are flagged, never silently deleted.
Shared corner and top stair posts use stable component references and are counted once in the model and any later takeoff.
Wood railing gates are a future, separately approved add-on; not included now (Q6).

openItems.item: Lumber merchant/vendor, species, grade/species combinations, stock lengths, brown-treated product and treatment details.
Round black aluminum baluster and matched connectors, finish and diameter.
1-1/2 in round satin-black graspable metal handrail product, mounting and return parts; whether 'Westburry' offers it.
Post anchoring for outside-rim, inside-rim and inside/outside stair posts; blocking, hold-downs, fasteners, post-spacing and rail-span limits; shared corner and top stair post loading.
Guard and stair opening rules, post/guard loads, handrail height range, graspable clearance, terminations and stair-side requirements per current code and product approvals.
Reviewed in-deck 4x4 guard-post detail: blocking, hold-down hardware, clearances and post-to-rim connection. Do not reuse outside-rim (face-mount) details without review (D-02).

compatibilityQuestions: Aluminum connectors on a vertical 2x4 rail: the connectors would mount to the 1-1/2 in narrow edge. Confirm the chosen connector fits that face.

Handrail projection: Minnesota limits handrail projection into the stair to 4.5 in per side (MN Rule 1309.0311). The 4x4 post (plus inside stair-post placement, if chosen) and stand-off bracket depth together need checking against stair width.
Handrail product: Westbury's ADA Handrail page publishes no diameter, black finish or stand-off bracket, so the 1-1/2 in satin-black round spec is not yet matched to a product.

Shared top stair post: a face-mounted deck post and an outside- or inside-mounted stair post may sit in different planes. Sharing works only where geometry lines up; otherwise the spec's separate top post applies.

Stair guard height 36/42 in from nosings is within the commonly cited 34 in minimum for stair guards (secondary source); a 36 in handrail is within the commonly cited 34-38 in range. Confirm against the ICC text.
Stair openings: 3-3/4 in clear spacing is measured on level runs. On sloped stair runs, openings and the triangle under the bottom rail need checking against stair opening rules.
Exposed posts with a T-top 2x6 cap: the cap must break at each post, and post caps (flat or pyramid) sit above the cap line. The visual model needs to show this per section.
Brown default with composite/PVC decking assumes brown-treated railing lumber is available from the AOS supplier (see owner-entered notes).

Current app post geometry (R1 rail inset, core chat note claude/aos-v53-r1-railing-review-items-for-c7.md): 2.52 in posts standing on the decking 1-1/2 in inside the finished edge (RAIL_FACE_INSET). D4 wood posts are nominal 4x4 (about 3-1/2 in actual), either on the outside rim face or inside the rim framing through the decking, so wood railing needs its own post placement per mounting rather than the shared inset.

Stair clear width: the app already raises a review alert below 36 in between post faces on 3 ft stairs. Wider 4x4 posts (especially inside-mounted stair posts) plus the inside-face handrail on stand-off brackets reduce clear width further; check the 3 ft default stair against both.
